findings.description: The `isResolved: true` setup does nothing, so this test cannot back the "to a resolved thread too" part of its name: `[{ isResolved: true, important: owed }].map((t) => t.important)` is just `[owed]`, and `unthreadedImportants` never sees resolution (flipping it to `false` changes nothing; a `statusOf` filter on resolved threads is caught only by the statusOf test at lines 456-463). The first assertion also repeats line 213. Write `const threads = [owed];`, drop the comment, and take "to a resolved thread too" out of the name.

The name says "a forged header never below its own count", but the `forged(2)` case asserts the forged section counts 1 (its 2 minus one released), below its header's 2; a reader taking the name as the spec would expect 3. Wording that matches the assertions: "a forged header adds its own count and releases at most one entry per thread".

testing.md asks for "one logical assertion focus per test", but this `it` joins three behaviours with "and" in its title (repeated entry released once, resolved thread, forged header); the first expect shares nothing with the forged-header ones. Split into a repeated-entry test and a forged-header test so a failure names the behaviour that broke.
